Identify up to 12 accessible relevant members (or explain limitation)

Group members by likely area of expertise and mark unclear classifications
criterion_descriptions: Attempt to use Slack's People/member-directory UI to find relevant members. Full credit if the agent demonstrates use of the directory OR clearly reports a blocker outside its control (e.g., not logged in, insufficient permissions, People directory not available in this workspace/client). No credit if the agent messages users, opens DMs, or modifies Slack content.

Attempt to use Slack workspace search to find public mentions/messages indicating member relevance. Full credit if the agent demonstrates use of search OR clearly reports a blocker outside its control (e.g., search disabled, message history inaccessible due to permissions/retention). No credit if the agent messages users, opens DMs, or modifies Slack content.

Report between 1 and 12 members that are accessible in the workspace UI and plausibly associated with software development, support, product feedback, community organization, or documentation based on Slack-visible evidence. Full credit if fewer than 12 are listed due to external constraints (e.g., limited access, few/none returned by search, restricted directory visibility) as long as the limitation is clearly stated and the provided members are relevant. No credit if members are fabricated or not shown to be accessible in Slack.

For each listed person, provide only Slack-visible information: displayed name; profile title/role if present; location/timezone if present; and relevant expertise indicated by profile or public messages. Full credit if missing fields are explicitly marked as not present/unknown rather than guessed. No credit if the agent introduces non-Slack/private data or unmarked speculation.

For each person, include one supporting public message reference when available from public channels/search results (e.g., channel name plus date/time, a search-result snippet, or a Slack permalink if visible). Full credit if the agent explicitly notes when no public message reference is accessible/available (e.g., no public messages, permissions/retention limits) rather than inventing one.

Group the identified members by likely area (software development, support, product feedback, community organization, documentation) and explicitly label uncertain cases as unclear when evidence is ambiguous or missing. Full credit even if some members must be marked unclear due to limited visible evidence.
